title: How Not to Lose Money

cards.aki: I have seen a lot of people lose money in crypto. Let's make sure you are not one of them.
cards.title: How Not to Lose Money
text: Six habits that keep beginners in the game: start small, skip perps, avoid meme gambling, pick good sources, ignore moon promises, and spot scams.

cards.aki: Rule one is boring, and it works.
cards.title: Start small
points: Only put in money you could lose without it hurting your rent, bills or sleep.
Make your first purchase tiny. Treat it as the price of learning.
Send a small test amount before any big transfer.
Buying a little on a regular schedule beats betting everything at once.

cards.title: You just learned about crypto. How much should you put in first?

options.text: Most of my savings, to make it worth it
options.why: Big bets while you are still learning are how most beginners lose money.

options.text: A small amount I can afford to lose
options.why: Yes. Small stakes let you learn the ropes without real damage.

options.text: Borrowed money, so I keep my savings
options.why: Never borrow to buy crypto. You can lose the money and still owe it.

cards.aki: Perps look like a shortcut. They are a trap for beginners.
cards.title: Why perps wreck beginners

items.back: At 20x, a 5 percent move against you wipes you out. Crypto moves 5 percent before lunch.
When you hit your limit, your position is closed automatically, often at the worst moment.
Holding a position costs you a fee every few hours, which eats your money even when price goes nowhere.

items.front: Who is on the other side
items.back: Professional traders and bots with better tools. Most retail perp traders lose.

cards.aki: Memecoins are fun to watch and painful to hold.
cards.title: Do not gamble on memecoins
points: Thousands launch every day, and most go to zero within days.
Bots and insiders buy first and sell to the crowd that arrives later.
Rug pulls: creators pull the money out and disappear.
The few big winners are the stories you hear. You never hear about the thousands of losers.
cards.tip: If you play anyway, use only what you would spend on a night out, and expect to lose it.

cards.aki: Who you listen to decides how you invest.
cards.title: Good sources versus noise

items.back: A project's own docs, blog and announcements, reached through its real website.
Tools like Etherscan show what actually happened onchain, instead of what someone claims.

items.front: Good: people who show their work
items.back: Researchers and writers who explain their reasoning, share risks, and admit when they were wrong.
Anonymous gem calls, screenshots of gains, and anyone who never mentions risk.

cards.aki: Be careful with anyone promising the moon.
cards.title: Ignore KOLs promising the moon
text: KOL means key opinion leader: an influencer with a big following. Many are paid to promote tokens, often without saying so, and some sell to their own followers.
points: Words like guaranteed, next 100x or last chance.
Rushing you to buy right now.
Never talking about risk or losses.
cards.tip: If someone is sure a coin will moon, ask yourself why they are telling thousands of strangers.

cards.aki: Scammers are creative. These are the ones you will meet first.
cards.title: Spot common scams

steps.label: Fake support
steps.text: Someone posing as support messages you first. Real support never DMs first and never asks for your seed phrase.

steps.label: Fake websites
steps.text: Lookalike addresses and ads that lead to copies of real sites. Use bookmarks, not search ads.

steps.label: Wallet drainers
steps.text: Claim an airdrop pages that ask you to sign or approve. One signature can empty your wallet.

steps.label: Send 1, get 2
steps.text: Fake giveaways using famous faces. Nobody doubles your crypto.

steps.label: Pig butchering
steps.text: A friendly stranger builds trust for weeks, then guides you to a fake trading app that never lets you withdraw.

cards.title: A 'support agent' DMs you a link to fix a problem with your wallet. What do you do?

options.text: Click it quickly before the problem gets worse
options.why: The rush is the trick. The link leads to a fake site.

options.text: Ignore it, block them, and get help only through the official app
options.why: Right. Real support never messages you first.

options.text: Reply to ask if they are real
options.why: Scammers will always say yes. Do not engage.

cards.aki: Stick to these and you will already beat most beginners.
cards.title: Quick recap
points: Start small, and only with money you can afford to lose.
Skip perps and leverage while you are learning.
Memecoins are a casino. Treat them that way, or skip them.
Follow sources that show their work, and check onchain.
Nobody legit DMs first, asks for your seed phrase or doubles your money.
